stack.ui: Interactive Server for board surfaces, static SSR for auth and marketing
stack.hosting: On-premises: Docker Compose primary, Windows Server + IIS secondary

document.note: Descriptive only. No application code is included, and no command in this file has been executed as part of producing the documentation.

decisions.rationale: Only supported stable runtime; .NET 11 is RC3 with GA 2026-11-10 and is STS; .NET 8 and 9 leave support on 2026-11-10.

decisions.decision: EF Core 10 + MySQL via Oracle MySql.EntityFrameworkCore 10.0.12
decisions.rationale: Owner choice of MySQL; Pomelo has no EF Core 10 release (issue 2007 open, latest stable 9.0.0 on EF Core 9).
decisions.risk: GPLv2 with FOSS exception requires a commercial connector licence for closed-source distribution (Q1).

decisions.decision: Blazor Web App, Interactive Server for board surfaces, static SSR elsewhere
decisions.rationale: Dense stateful grid; SignalR required regardless; no WebAssembly payload.

decisions.decision: On-premises Docker Compose primary, Windows Server + IIS secondary
Core recipes + multi-action + scheduled triggers, no marketplace
decisions.rationale: Behavioural parity with documented trigger/condition/action model without marketplace economics.
Legal defensibility; no source, assets, trademarks or trade dress.

phases.name: Foundations and walking skeleton
phases.objective: A repository that builds, starts, reports health, logs with correlation, and deploys to both target hosts.
scope: Seven projects per architecture section 3.1, all targeting net10.0
Layered configuration with fail-fast startup validation
MySQL and Redis containers for local development
Structured logging with correlation id and OpenTelemetry traces
Health endpoints live and ready
CI: restore, build, unit test, licence scan, secret scan
outOfScope: Any UI beyond one static page

slice.description: The app starts from a clean clone, /health/ready reports MySQL and Redis reachable, and one static SSR page renders visible content.
commands: docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d mysql redis
observableChecks: Browser shows the page content, not an empty shell
GET /health/live returns healthy
GET /health/ready returns healthy with both dependencies
One log line carries a correlation id
Response headers show the expected content types for CSS and JS

exitCriteria: Release build succeeds with zero warnings
All unit tests pass
Both health endpoints green
Static page verified by screenshot, not by HTTP status
CI green on a clean checkout
phases.validationGate: Operator confirms the app starts on their target host path and the health page is reachable.

phases.name: Identity, tenancy and workspaces
phases.objective: Four roles, proven tenant isolation, workspaces, board shells and grants.
scope: OpenIddict authorization server with cookie session and PATs
ASP.NET Core Identity user store, TOTP MFA
Account, Membership, tenant context, global query filter, write interceptor
Permission snapshot and resource-based policies
Workspace, folder, visibility rules, board shell, board grants
Circuit security-stamp revalidation
Isolation suite and capability matrix tests
dependencies: Open question Q4 (guest visibility of subitems) before the grant model hardens

slice.description: Sign in, create a workspace, create a board shell, invite a viewer, and prove a guest receives 404 for an ungranted board.
commands: dotnet ef migrations add InitialTenancy --project src/Tuesday.Infrastructure
dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent --project src/Tuesday.Infrastructure --output artifacts/schema.sql
observableChecks: Sign-in redirects to the workspace and the session survives a refresh
Invited viewer sees the board read-only, with no edit affordance
Guest sees only the granted board; other board URLs return 404
Role change takes effect on a live session within 60 seconds
Audit rows exist for tenant creation, invite and grant

exitCriteria: All eight isolation tests green
Full capability matrix green for four roles
Viewer cannot obtain a usable API token
No production code path calls IgnoreQueryFilters outside the tenancy module
phases.validationGate: An operator signs in as each of the four roles and confirms each sees exactly what the capability table promises.

phases.name: Boards, groups, columns and the item grid
phases.objective: A usable board: columns, groups, items, subitems and a fast, keyboard-operable grid.
scope: Schema for Board, BoardColumn, ItemGroup, Item, ItemColumnValue and projections
Single value-writer path maintaining JSON and typed projections
Virtualised grid with inline edit, keyboard model, drag reorder, multi-select
Subitems with their own column structure and copy-not-sync semantics
P2 column type set
100k-item performance checkpoint
dependencies: Q1 (MySQL connector licence) resolution before external distribution

slice.description: Build a board with eight columns, three groups and 500 items; edit a cell inline; reload and see the value persisted.
commands: dotnet ef migrations add BoardCore --project src/Tuesday.Infrastructure
observableChecks: Cell edit shows immediately and survives a hard reload
Keyboard-only edit works: Tab, arrows, Enter, Escape, focus retained
Drag a row within a group and across groups; siblings keep their position keys
Subitem expansion shows its own column headers; editing the parent does not change the subitem
Adding the 501st column is refused with a typed error
Board page loads under 1.5 s p95 at 5,000 items

exitCriteria: A user builds and uses a real board for 30 minutes without a blocker
NFR-1 met at 5,000 items; 100k checkpoint under 3 s with no filesort
Projection consistency suite green on 1,000 sampled rows
UI evidence gates G-UI-1 to G-UI-7 satisfied for the board route
phases.validationGate: A real user models their actual work on the board for half an hour and reports no blocking gap.

phases.name: Views: Kanban, Calendar, Timeline, Gantt
phases.objective: Four real projections of the same board data, each with a persisted drag interaction.
scope: Kanban with status-only grouping, divide-by, empty-lane hiding, cover and card columns
Calendar placement by date column with month and week modes
Timeline with two-date bars and drag reschedule
Gantt with dependency arrows and cycle refusal
Remaining column types including location, country, doc, dependency, board_relation, checkbox, button and read-only types
View limit enforcement at 100 per board
outOfScope: Workload, map, form, pivot and blank views

slice.description: The same board rendered as Kanban, Calendar, Timeline and Gantt, with one drag in each view that persists after reload.
observableChecks: Kanban columns match status labels exactly, and an empty lane is hidden when the option is on
Calendar places items on their date column and switches month to week
Timeline bar drag changes the start date and survives reload
Gantt draws dependency arrows; creating a dependency cycle is refused
Adding the 101st view is refused
Contrast passes AA in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit

exitCriteria: Each view is a live projection with at least one persisted interaction
No view duplicates data storage; all writes go through the value writer
Accessibility checks clean on all four views across the three engines
phases.validationGate: A user who works in Kanban confirms they would use this view instead of a spreadsheet.

phases.name: Collaboration: updates, notifications, search
phases.objective: People can discuss work, be notified, and find things, with real-time delivery.
scope: Updates with sanitised HTML, replies and likes
In-app notifications, email via SMTP, preferences and subscriptions
FULLTEXT search over item names and update bodies, permission filtered
Attachments with signed URLs and expiry
Presence and reconnect-by-version

slice.description: Post an update on an item from one browser, see it appear in a second browser without refresh, receive a notification, and find the item by search.
commands: dotnet ef migrations add Collaboration --project src/Tuesday.Infrastructure
observableChecks: Update appears in the second browser within 2 seconds without refresh
Script payload in an update body is rendered inert
Reply and like counts are correct after reload
Notification appears in the bell and an email is queued
Search finds a term in an item name and in an update body
Search never returns an item from a board the user cannot see

exitCriteria: Two users on two browsers see each other's updates live
Search respects permissions under the isolation suite
Attachment signed URL expires and is rejected afterwards
phases.validationGate: A team runs a real stand-up on the product for one week.

phases.name: Automations, webhooks and public API
phases.objective: The product does work by itself and exposes an integration surface an outsider can use with documentation only.
scope: Recipe model with trigger, conditions and ordered multi-actions
Trigger registry, condition evaluator, action executor, loop guard, quota metering
Quartz cluster with recurring and date-arrival triggers
Outbound webhooks with challenge handshake, HMAC signing, retries and auto-disable
REST API v1 with cursor pagination, idempotency keys, cost model and OpenAPI snapshot
SSRF guard on webhook registration and delivery
dependencies: Q2 (GraphQL) and Q3 (date-arrival timezone) answered before engine hardening

slice.description: The worked example recipe fires end to end (status becomes Done, owner notified, subitem created), and an external endpoint receives a signed webhook after completing the challenge handshake.
commands: dotnet ef migrations add Automation --project src/Tuesday.Infrastructure
observableChecks: Recipe fires on status change, notifies the owner, and creates the follow-up subitem
A failing webhook action does not stop the following notification action
A self-triggering recipe stops at depth 3 and records LoopPrevented
Over-quota execution is refused before any action runs
Webhook is not delivered until the challenge is echoed
Tampered body and stale timestamp are rejected by the receiver test harness
The 1,001st daily call on a Standard-tier tenant is refused with retry_in_seconds
Repeating a request with the same Idempotency-Key produces one side effect

exitCriteria: The worked example fires end to end with an auditable run log
An external integrator succeeds using only the API documentation
OpenAPI snapshot diff clean; no breaking change inside v1
All P5 checklist items in the acceptance manual satisfied
phases.validationGate: A non-author integrates one real external system without help from the build team.

phases.name: Dashboards, hardening and on-prem release
phases.objective: Something an operator can install from scratch, back up, roll back and trust.
scope: Dashboard with chart, count and list widgets, permission-aware
CSP and security headers, dependency and licence closure, SBOM
Performance soak at 200 users and a 5,000-item board
Backup, restore and rollback rehearsals
Second-replica checklist: shared key ring, affinity, WebSockets
Compose bundle, IIS deployment guide, upgrade and runbook set
outOfScope: Enterprise SSO unless Q6 says otherwise

slice.description: A dashboard with three widgets over a live board, deployed to the target host, with a backup restored into a scratch environment and a rollback from N+1 to N demonstrated.
observableChecks: Dashboard widgets reflect live board data and respect viewer permissions
WebSocket upgrade succeeds at the proxy, not a long-poll fallback
Two web replicas share the key ring; no random sign-outs during a 10-minute soak
Backup restored into a scratch instance serves a working board
Rollback to the previous image restores sign-in and a working write path
Security headers present; CSP enforced after a report-only week

exitCriteria: Operator installs from scratch using only the runbooks
Backup, restore and rollback each demonstrated once by the operator
Performance targets met at 200 users
Licence register clean or Q1 resolved
SBOM archived with the release
Clean-room CI scans active and green
phases.validationGate: Operator installs on a clean host and runs a real workload for one week before 1.0 sign-off.

crossPhaseGates.gate: UI evidence G-UI-1 to G-UI-7 on changed routes
crossPhaseGates.evidence: screenshot plus console and asset diagnostics

crossPhaseGates.gate: Accessibility: no serious or critical violations on changed pages
Clean-room scans clean (banned strings, assets, screenshots)

totals.calendarEstimate: 5 to 7 months for a four-person team including a dedicated tester

openQuestions.question: Is the Oracle MySQL connector licence purchased, or does distribution stay internal-only?
openQuestions.default: internal-only deployment; licence tracked as release blocker

openQuestions.question: REST only, or REST plus GraphQL?
Is date-arrival evaluated in tenant timezone or per-user timezone?
May guests see subitems of a granted item?
Retention period for audit and automation-run history?
Will a hosted multi-tenant edition ever be required?
